stories.headline: Tool and target: US law enforcement grapple with AI-enabled terrorism and anti-tech extremism
stories.script: Around the world. From the FBI to local police departments, US authorities are increasingly warning of would-be terrorists using chatbots to plan attacks and anti-AI extremist threats In May 2025, a 25-year-old man detonated a car bomb outside a Palm Springs fertility clinic, killing himself and injuring four others. For many, it was a wake-up call about the threats to reproductive care facilities. For the FBI, though, it was also a sign of what the agency had feared for years: bad actors were using generative AI to plan and execute terror plots. The suspect used an unnamed generative AI tool that failed to detect his request for bomb-making instructions, law enforcement officers wrote in a previously unreported document reviewed by the Guardian.

stories.headline: VideoJev: System One Model for Video Understanding and Interaction
stories.script: Also today. Visual agents must turn video observations into timely decisions to track progress and choose what to do next. Building on the emerging System One paradigm, the researchers introduce VideoJev, a family of models that cast video understanding and interaction as structured decision tasks. The researchers adapt pretrained multimodal large language models (MLLMs) by replacing autoregressive answer decoding with a shared head that scores temporal intervals and textual options against video evidence. These scores yield event spans or answer choices, unifying temporal grounding and multiple-choice video question answering. This combines the semantic flexibility of MLLMs with efficient decisions that agents can use directly. As an interaction unfolds, new goals and intermediate results prompt further queries about the same visual history. VideoJev therefore reuses visual computation through Cached inference for queries as they arrive and Joint inference for multiple queries in a single forward pass.
stories.whyThisMatters: Visual agents must turn video observations into timely decisions to track progress and choose what to do next.
keyPoints: VideoJev: System One Model for Video Understanding and Interaction

stories.headline: Square’s new kiosk lets you talk to AI for help with your order
stories.script: Turning to the United States. Square is launching new hardware: a big kiosk for ordering things that has a touchscreen and lets you talk to an AI. Square says the Kiosk, which has a large pill shape, has an "agentic, conversational voice layer" that "fully understands a seller's menu and listens and responds in real time, enabling customers to order the way they'd naturally talk to staff." While talking with the AI agent, you can do things like ask questions and request modifications and substitutions. The touchscreen on the Kiosk is 21.5 inches, and the device can welcome you as you approach thanks to presence detection, Square says.
